final_report: T17.7 done, commit f4b0c62 (feat(learning): notes quiz grounded in source environments) on feature/latex-notes. app/llm/notes.py (161 lines): request_notes_questions(llm, *, session, seed_chunks, count, subject) generates ONE question per seed chunk (up to count) via a single complete_json call each with the chunk as the only [SEED SOURCE] block, so source_ref is deterministic (built by _source_ref from the chunk, never echoed by the model); the prompt encodes the KNIGHT criteria (correct option near-verbatim restatement, unambiguity, near-miss distractors: swapped hypotheses/misapplied conditions/common errors) and the unicode-math rule ('write math in unicode only (e.g. alpha, integral, sqrt) — never raw LaTeX such as \alpha, \int, or \frac'); parse tolerance mirrors structured.py (_try_parse + one corrective retry, provider errors raise via provider_error_from_text, fragments dropped); verify_answerability(llm, question, seed_text) makes up to two complete_json calls asking whether the correct option is literally supported by the source block ({"supported": bool}), returning False on provider failure, parse failure, or retry failure — unsupported questions are dropped.
